scene: Inferno XVII — Geryon inspected, usurers seen, descent into Malebolge
story: Geryon comes to the edge of the abyss, displaying the face of an honest man while concealing a serpentine, intricately patterned body and a poisonous scorpion tail.
Virgil identifies Geryon as the monstrous image of fraud and asks Dante to inspect the usurers nearby while he arranges passage.
Dante sees seated usurers on the burning sand bearing purses marked with emblems and returns to Virgil.
Virgil instructs Dante to climb onto Geryon's back in front of him; Dante boards in fear while Virgil positions himself to guard against the tail.
Geryon backs away from the edge and circles through the air, descending into the eighth circle, Malebolge.
They land at the bottom. Virgil and Dante dismount; Geryon departs.
